cases.question: Our SaaS receives webhooks from a payment processor. Today we verify an HMAC-SHA256 signature using a shared secret and accept any timestamp. The webhook handler updates user balances. Threat-model this endpoint — what are the highest-severity attack paths and how should we harden it?

Users upload PDFs to our app, and we render thumbnails server-side using a headless Chromium pool. The renderer runs as a non-root user in a Docker container with no network egress. Where are the attack paths an adversary could chain end-to-end? Be specific about preconditions.

We issue JWTs signed with HS256 using a single application-wide secret. Tokens contain user_id and role claims and have a 24-hour expiry. Refresh tokens are stored in an HttpOnly cookie. What's the strongest attack against this design and what are the top three mitigations?
